narrative:
The model predicts a 90% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the fact that you have received other job offers, and the relatively short time you have spent in your current role. 

Your six to ten years of total experience was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only one to five years of experience, your mid-level career stage appears to give you more external options, making departure more likely in the model's view. The presence of other job opportunities was the second-biggest driver, strongly increasing the chance of leaving because most employees who stay do not report receiving such offers. Finally, having spent only one to five years in your current organization also nudged the prediction toward leaving, as longer tenure in one place is more common among those expected to remain.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be at a natural career point where moving on feels attractive. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You might consider what would make staying worthwhile, such as clearer advancement paths or better recognition of your experience. Addressing these areas could change the outlook for both sides.
